about.title: About {brand}
about.lead: {brand} helps licence plates lost in floods get back to their owners. Owners register the plate number, finders send a photo, and we match them. Free, with no ads.

owner.a: Tap “I lost a plate”, type the plate number and choose the province.
owner.b: If someone has already found it, you see it straight away. Compare the photo with your plate, then get the finder’s contact details.
owner.c: If not, add your contact details and report it lost. When someone finds it, it is matched automatically. Check “My posts” for matches (sign in with Google to see them on another device).

finder.a: Tap “I found a plate” and take a photo. One photo can hold several plates.
finder.b: Plates are found and read automatically. If one is missed, drag a box around it and tap “Add this plate”. Always check the number and province.
finder.c: Add your contact details and send. If the owner has reported it lost, you see the owner’s contact details.
finder.d: Return the plate yourself, or hand it in at a police station.

handover.a: If anyone asks you to transfer money before you have the plate back, don’t pay.
handover.b: Owners bring the registration book and ID card; finders ask to see them before handing over.
handover.c: Meet in a public place or at a police station.

terms.title: Terms of use

items.a: {brand} is a free, non-profit service that only matches plate numbers. We never hold, collect or deliver plates.
items.b: We do not verify who users are. Check for yourself before meeting or handing over a plate. We are not liable for loss or harm from contact or handovers between users.
items.c: Post only true details of a plate you lost or found. No false posts, scams, demands for money, or using someone’s contact details for anything else.
items.d: Finders should return plates to their owners or hand them to the police.
items.e: Automatic plate reading can be wrong; check before sending. The service is provided as is and may pause at times.
items.f: We may hide or remove posts that break these terms, and may update the terms; the date of the last update is shown on this page.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: {brand} collects only the personal data it needs to get licence plates back to their owners. This policy explains what we collect, why, who can see it, how long we keep it, and your rights under Thailand’s Personal Data Protection Act B.E. 2562 (2019).

items.a: The data controller under this policy is the operator of {brand}, operating as {operator}. You can reach us at {email}.
2.1 What you enter when posting: the plate number, province, plate type, a note, and any contact details you choose to give (LINE ID, phone number or email).
items.b: 2.2 Plate photos. A finder’s photo is cropped to the plate on their own device before it is sent, so we only ever receive the cropped plate, never the full photo. Data embedded in the photo, such as GPS location, is removed.
items.c: 2.3 Google account details, only if you choose to sign in: your account ID and email address. We never receive your password and do not ask for access to anything else in your account.
items.d: 2.4 Technical data. Your IP address is turned into a code that changes every day before it is stored; we never store the IP address itself. The code is used to limit unusually frequent submissions, prevent spam, and record when contact details are viewed.
items.e: 2.5 Feedback and reports: the rating and comments you send through the feedback form, and the reason you give when reporting a post.
items.f: 2.6 We do not collect your name, national ID number, bank account number or location, and our forms will not accept them.

s3.title: 3. Why we use it, and on what legal basis

items.a: 3.1 To match plates reported lost with plates that have been found, and to let matched users contact each other, based on the consent you give before posting.
items.b: 3.2 To let you manage your own posts (extend, close or delete them) and link them to your Google account when you sign in, as part of providing the service you asked for.
items.c: 3.3 To prevent misuse, spam and scams and to keep the system secure, based on our legitimate interests and those of other users.
items.d: 3.4 To improve the service using feedback and aggregated usage statistics that do not identify anyone.
items.e: 3.5 To comply with the law or with orders from authorities empowered by law.

items.a: 4.1 Your contact details are shown only to users the system matches with your post, and only after they confirm they have read our scam warning.
items.b: 4.2 Lost-plate posts never appear in search results. Photos of found plates are shown to people who search for that plate number, without any contact details.
items.c: 4.3 We rely on outside providers, who can access data only as far as their role requires: Supabase (database, photo storage and user accounts), Vercel (website hosting), Cloudflare Turnstile (bot protection) and Google (sign-in).
items.d: 4.4 We do not sell, rent or trade your personal data, and we do not use it for advertising.
items.e: 4.5 We may disclose data where the law requires it or under an order from a court or competent authority.

items.a: The servers of the providers listed in 4.3 may be located outside Thailand, so your data may be stored or processed abroad. We choose providers with internationally recognised data protection measures, and any transfer abroad is made under the conditions set by the Personal Data Protection Act.

6.1 Posts, contact details and plate photos last {days} days from the day they are posted. The owner of a post can extend it by {extendDays} days at a time, up to {maxDays} days in total. When a post expires or you delete it, this data is deleted from the system.
items.b: 6.2 Records of contact details being viewed: 30 days.
items.c: 6.3 Feedback sent through the form: up to 1 year.
items.d: 6.4 Data used to limit frequent submissions: up to 2 days.
items.e: 6.5 Google account details: until you ask us to delete your account.
items.f: 6.6 Where the law requires us to keep some data for longer, we keep it only as long as the law requires.

items.a: 7.1 We only use the cookies and browser storage the service needs to work. There are no advertising cookies and no third-party tracking cookies.
items.b: 7.2 These are: a cookie remembering the language you chose, sign-in cookies (only while you are signed in), and browser storage that remembers which posts were made from this device, the colour theme you picked, and anything you have half-filled in a form.
items.c: 7.3 Cloudflare Turnstile may process technical data from your browser to tell real people from bots.
items.d: 7.4 If you delete cookies or browser data, you will be signed out and may no longer be able to manage posts you made without signing in.

items.a: We take reasonable measures to prevent unauthorised access, use or disclosure, including HTTPS encryption, restricted database access, keeping photos in private storage that can only be opened through short-lived links, and converting IP addresses before storing them. No system is completely secure, however. If a personal data breach occurs, we will act on it and notify as the law requires.

9.1 Under the Personal Data Protection Act B.E. 2562, you have the right to access and obtain a copy of your data, to have it corrected, to have it deleted or destroyed, to restrict its use, to object to its processing, to have it transferred, and to withdraw your consent at any time.
items.b: 9.2 Withdrawing consent does not affect processing already carried out. Once you withdraw it, we delete your posts and stop showing your contact details, which means the system can no longer match your plate.
items.c: 9.3 You can delete or close your own posts straight away on the “My posts” page. For any other request, including deleting your account, email {email}. We will reply within 30 days of receiving your request and may ask for more information to confirm the data is yours.
items.d: 9.4 If you believe we have not complied with personal data protection law, you have the right to complain to the Office of the Personal Data Protection Committee.

items.a: The service is not aimed at collecting data from minors. Minors who wish to use it should first have a parent’s or guardian’s consent. If a parent or guardian finds that a minor has submitted data without consent, let us know and we will delete it.

We may update this policy as the service and the law change. The last-updated date is shown on this page. For material changes, especially using data for a new purpose, we will give notice on the website and ask for your consent again where the law requires.
Send any question or request about your personal data to {email}.
